title: Art & Music
text: In Delphine’s practice, the concept operates as an originary force, an immanent logic that precedes and determines its own conditions of material instantiation. The medium does not pre-exist the work but is called forth by the idea itself, such that photography, video art and film emerge not as discrete disciplinary choices but as contingent modalities through which thought achieves its sensible form. The artwork, in this sense, is less an object than an event of mediation between concept and matter.

Current work

In progress

Evaluating large language models with political psychology scales
I’m investigating how we evaluate large language models using established political psychology scales: what it means for a model to “hold” a political attitude, and how far the measurement tools built for people can be trusted when they are applied to AI.

title: About me
text:
Hi, I’m Delphine, a Vietnamese artist and researcher-in-training based in Sydney.
My research brings together political theory, data science and statistical methods, with interests spanning computational international relations, predictive modelling and machine learning. I’m particularly interested in how we measure political beliefs, and what those measurements can tell us. Right now, I’m part of the Data Impact Lab under the guidance of Dr Jie Kang, and I’m investigating how we evaluate large language models using established political psychology scales.
Alongside my research, I act, sing and write songs, and I produce art films, music, commercials and narrative films. My creative and academic practices inform each other, offering different ways to explore questions of politics, identity and power.

title: About me
text:
Biography
Delphine PA Dang is a Vietnamese artist, musician and researcher in Sydney. She approaches art and creative work through her close relationship with data science and statistics, and with international relations, political theory and political thought. Her intellectual focus spans political theory, computational international relations and psychometrics, and her artistic practice is strongly research-oriented: her latest film, An Eye for an I, turns her findings on large language models into an audiovisual work.
Beyond her primary creative pursuits, Delphine practises acting, composing and singing. In collaboration, she takes on the roles of producer, composer-vocalist, assistant director and strategic manager to realise the visions of artists and brands. Her work as editor on the music video Be My East (dir. Gavin Goh) won Best Cinematography at the Sony Catchlight Festival 2026.
Delphine trained in opera singing for seven years, an undertaking that began after she won the Golden Buzzer on Vietnam’s Got Talent, the moment that marked the start of her professional vocal training. Alongside opera, she plays bass and has a background in ballet, theatre and acting. These performative disciplines inform her wider artistic sensibility, shaping how she approaches composition, presence and narrative across her visual and research-driven work.
